questions.q: In the Help Desk Ticket app, why does a Dynamic Form hide the Asset__c field until Priority__c is set?
options: Dynamic Forms can only show lookup fields last
Asset__c is a required field on every object by default
What broke only matters once severity has been triaged, so showing it earlier is unnecessary clutter
Priority__c cannot be set unless Asset__c is already populated
questions.explain: This mirrors the course's UX principle (Chapter 4, Lesson 22): show only the fields relevant to the record's current state, reducing clutter and clicks.

questions.q: In the Escalate quick action, what is the relationship between the screen Flow and the approval process?
options: They are unrelated; the Flow replaces the approval process entirely
The Flow sets Priority__c to Critical, which is what triggers the approval process's entry criteria — the Flow decides when, the approval process still does the routing
The approval process triggers the Flow, not the other way around
The Flow and approval process both run independently with no connection
questions.explain: This is the Lesson 17 pattern reused: Flow handles the decision logic (setting Priority to Critical), and the purpose-built approval process handles the actual human routing.

questions.q: What does the roll-up summary field on Asset__c in this app calculate?
options: The total dollar cost of all tickets
The average resolution time across all technicians
The number of technicians assigned to the help desk
A count of open Help_Desk_Ticket__c records related to that asset
questions.explain: The roll-up summary counts open tickets per asset, directly from the master-detail (or equivalent) relationship between Asset__c and Help_Desk_Ticket__c.

questions.q: What security configuration ensures the IT Queue has read/write access to all Help_Desk_Ticket__c records, given a Private org-wide default?
options: A sharing rule granting the IT Queue access, since OWD alone defaults to the most restrictive setting
A validation rule granting access based on Priority
Raising the org-wide default to Public Read/Write instead
A roll-up summary field configured for sharing
questions.explain: With Private OWD as the strict baseline, a sharing rule is the declarative tool that grants the additional access the IT Queue actually needs.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what Flow capability did the Help Desk Ticket capstone deliberately NOT use, leaving it for the next course in the path?
options: Formula fields
Record-triggered Flow, loops, collections, subflows, and scheduled processing
Validation rules
Change sets
questions.explain: The capstone used only a short screen Flow triggering an approval. Deeper Flow capabilities — record-triggered automation, loops, collections, subflows, scheduling — are explicitly left for the Flow Automation course that follows.
